title: Specification
body:
Step four of [[Software Requirements Analysis]]: write the requirements down precisely enough
that the system can be built from them and tested against them. The document is the contract
between the people who want the system and the people building it, and in [[Waterfall]] it is
literally treated as one, because the next phase is not allowed to question it.

What a specification has to be:

- **Complete** every requirement is in it, including the non-functional ones
- **Consistent** no two requirements contradict each other
- **Unambiguous** one reading only, which is why "should be fast" fails and "returns
  within two seconds" passes
- **Testable** every statement can be turned into a pass or fail
- **Traceable** each requirement can be followed forward into the design and the tests

Natural language is the default and is also the source of most ambiguity, which is why
[[Modeling]] happens first: a diagram forces decisions that prose lets you skip. The
specification is then checked in [[Review]], the last step, where the customer confirms this
is what they meant.

[[Project Success]] is measured against this document, so a vague one makes success
unmeasurable.
